scale: 0 to 5; manual design assessment, not automated test count

deductions.finding: Settings, Skills, ProductDetail, rarity cards and loading use different title, material, border and artwork-framing systems.
1,114 undersized live-text instances across the measured route matrix; small secondary copy and catalogue overflow reduce readability.
Income and instruction hierarchy are more compact than other screens, without shared type roles.
Retained legacy geometry overlaps skill names, effects and action columns; major defect, gate failed.
Home income overlaps and the goal text exceeds its row.
16 catalogue text overflow instances; remaining no-wrap geometry must be removed.
Earnings strip retains an obsolete fixed height; prototype not ready for native transfer.
Details button and compact timing spacing differ from the common action treatment.
Appearance illustrations are oversized; catalogue filter buttons retain narrow legacy widths.
Product overview contains leftover fixed geometry despite the common section shell.
Tutorial now shares common typography; width and helper-copy roles require compact-layout verification before gate.
Specialist content requires different section counts and two-line titles; all use the same component/type/material rules.
The full-stall requirement makes the lower Home area scroll on short screens. All actions reveal fully; the tradeoff adds one gesture.
Long purchase reviews and catalogue descriptions remain dense; pinned actions, readable type and scrolling preserve access.
Historic illustrations retain small texture differences; shared framing, palette, scale and typography unify their presentation.
Tall informational content requires more scrolling at the smallest viewport; no internal text clipping or lost controls remains.
Celebrations remain intentionally richer than ordinary navigation. Bounded effects and reduced-motion settling pass; perceptual sound quality is self-assessed.
